title: adaptive-scheduler-emission-jitter-hotpatch
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary:
Customer-facing TTFT spikes and tokens/sec variance observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after a recent scheduler/optimizer merge. Impact pattern is non-uniform: smaller contexts (<=128 tokens) saw higher first-token latency increases, long-context sessions observed throughput jitter. Customers reported intermittent degraded UX on chat and streaming routes.

What happened:
- Nightly rollout (runtime change set r1.20-sched-v2) introduced an adaptive scheduling heuristic intended to improve batch packing for heterogeneous GPU pools.
- In clusters with mixed GPU types (A100 + H100 mixes in Dedicated, and some Private customer VMs), scheduler micro-decisions cause small starvation windows during warmup. These windows disrupt token emission timing and expose a race in the token-streaming handshake subsystem, creating 200-1000ms TTFT spikes for some requests and variable tokens/sec on sustained sessions.

Investigation highlights and evidence:
- Correlated spike windows with scheduler decision events using trace_id; root cause trace: scheduler preemption + microbatch reorder -> delayed kernel launch for the first attention pass.
- Repro in staging with a heterogeneous node pool by toggling the adaptive-scheduler flag.
- Github PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 (scheduler) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4752 (reorder mitigation experiment).
- Customer escalations: Priority support threads  #cust-1134 and #cust-1178.
- Runbook and incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TTFT+Emission+Jitter+Incident

Mitigations applied so far:
- Immediate rollback of the adaptive scheduling heuristic to previous stable behavior in Hosted starting 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC; rollback in Dedicated and Private performed in coordination with impacted customers (manual flip of feature-flag).
- Short-term shim: introduced a scheduler-safe burst-hedge that prevents micro-preemption during the first attention pass (deployed to staging and small canary pool).
- Emergency customer rollouts: coordinated with three highest-impact customers to push rollback patches to their Private clusters.

Open work / proposed fix plan:
1) Stability patch (hotfix): eliminate the reorder race by making kernel launch decision idempotent for priming steps. Target: small code change + unit tests. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-03-18.
2) Improved scheduling heuristics: redesign adaptive logic to operate on epoch windows (less frequent decision boundaries) and include a priming-safe mode for heterogeneous pools. Owner: Systems team. ETA: 2026-04-01.
3) SLO coverage: add synthetic canary workload that mimics mixed-model, mixed-GPU fanout to detect this class of regressions in preflight. Owner: Observability. ETA: 2026-03-25.
4) Customer communication: publish incident summary, mitigations, and ETA for permanent fix. PM lead: Priya Kaur. ETA: 2026-03-16.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Keeping adaptive scheduler enabled improves throughput for large-batch workloads but introduces small risk windows for priming latency. The short-term decision was to favor latency SLOs (rollback) while we redesign the heuristic.
- A conservative scheduler reduces overall token-efficiency in certain synthetic benchmarks; we'll tune incentives in runtime-telemetry to recover cost without sacrificing priming stability.

Next steps (immediate):
- Complete and land the stability patch and run the canary (ENG-1009999-PT1).
- Push automated e2e test that reproduces the priming race (ENG-1009999-E2E).
- Finalize customer incident writeup and coordinate Dedicated/Private upgrade cadence.

Risks and monitoring:
- Risk of incomplete rollback in some edge Private installs (customers running pinned manifests). Need to validate manifests by 2026-03-17.
- Monitor first-byte and tokens/sec histograms for the next two weeks; set automated alerts for 95th percentile TTFT regressions vs baseline.

Artifacts:
- PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4809
- Canary dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ttft-emission-jitter/canary
updates: 2026-03-10: Issue opened after biz-hours escalation from two hosted customers. Initial triage assigned to Diego. Created canary to reproduce.
2026-03-11: Rolled back adaptive-scheduler feature flag in hosted. Canary showed immediate TTFT improvement. Patch candidate identified.
2026-03-12: Applied manual fixes for two Dedicated customers; Private customers notified and patch instructions shared. Still seeing rare spikes in small subset of test nodes.
2026-03-13: Root cause narrowed to kernel-launch/preemption race during priming; small hotfix PR opened (4809).
2026-03-15: Hotfix PR passed CI; canary on mixed-gpu pool shows 98% reduction in TTFT spike incidence. Preparing customer rollouts and postmortem.
Next: Complete automated e2e and push to runtime-1.20.1 release train.
